USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Replacing a lost mucosal defense

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An older patient needs continued NSAID therapy and has a high risk of gastric ulcer complications. Misoprostol is prescribed because it replaces a protective pathway diminished by cyclooxygenase inhibition. Which endogenous mediator does the drug most closely mimic?

  1. Prostaglandin E1
  2. Histamine
  3. Acetylcholine
  4. Gastrin
  5. Leukotriene D4
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Prostaglandin E1

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog with antisecretory and mucosal protective actions.

Understanding the options

Prostaglandin E1
Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog with antisecretory and mucosal protective actions.
Histamine
Histamine stimulates acid through H2 receptors.
Acetylcholine
Acetylcholine can stimulate gastric secretion and motility.
Gastrin
Gastrin stimulates acid secretion.
Leukotriene D4
Leukotrienes are not the protective prostaglandin pathway replaced.
